name: X++
title: X++ (10.0)

presenceList.meta: R2, R3, Ec4, Ec5, Ec6, Ec7, Ec8, D1, D3, L2, Q3

type.text: **A class and an interface state the contract**: X++ follows the .NET type system
**There are no sum types**: An enum or a base class plus a discriminator
**Reflection reaches the metadata**: .NET reflection reads a type at run time
**A reference can be null**: The type does not say whether it is set

construction.text: **`new` runs a constructor**: A class states its invariants
**A field is mutable by default**: A property is read/write unless the author restricts it

memory.text: **The CLR collects**: The pause is the runtime's
**There is no scope-exit release**: `try/finally` closes a resource
**There is no ownership model**: Aliasing is unrestricted

error.text: **There is no result type**: A failure is an exception

concurrency.text: **The batch framework runs a job**: A runnable class is scheduled by the platform
**Locks are manual**: `ttsbegin` and the transaction scope are the discipline

platform.text: **A program runs only in Dynamics 365**: The AOS, the database, and the metadata are the platform
**The runtime is the CLR**: X++ compiles to CIL and uses the .NET libraries

performance.text: **A collection pause is part of the timing**
**The database round trip dominates**: A loop over a table must be set-based
**The AOS caches metadata and data**: A hot path can avoid a round trip

ecosystem.text: **The platform is proprietary**: Microsoft licences the ERP and the toolchain
**The tooling is Visual Studio plus the Dynamics extension**: Deployment is the platform's
**One platform is the ecosystem**: An X++ program serves one ERP
**The base application is a compatibility surface**: An extension must respect it
**A deployable package binds to a platform release**: Microsoft documents it as a binary update for one platform release, and the environment that receives it cannot rebuild it [@msDeployablePackage]

evolution.text: **The platform is updated in release waves**: A program moves with a service update
**The base application changes under an extension**: A chain of command can break

domain.text: **The domain is ERP**: Finance, supply chain, and manufacturing
**The framework sets the architecture**: Forms, tables, and the SysOperation framework

learning.text: **The language and the ERP model are learned together**: Two bodies of knowledge at once

syntax.text: **The syntax is C-like**: Braces, classes, and a SQL-like `select`
**The embedded SQL is a dialect**: A `select` statement is part of the language

testing.text: **The SysTest framework runs a unit test**: A test class is a model element

security.text: **A dynamic query takes a string**: A query built from input is an injection path
**The role and duty model is enforced**: An entry point checks a privilege

reproducibility.text: **The deployable package is not reproducible**: The package embeds build metadata and paths, and two builds are not compared

supplychain.text: **A deployable package can be signed**: A certificate signs the package for deployment

tradeoffs: **The ERP model is the language's domain**: A table and a form are the unit of design
**The CLR is a real runtime**: The language inherits a mature collector and library
**The base application is both platform and constraint**: An extension is written against a moving base
**The release wave is the upgrade path**: A program moves when the service moves
verdict: X++ is a .NET language on one ERP: classes, interfaces, the CLR, and a SQL-like query language make it a capable business language, but the program runs only inside Dynamics 365, the framework sets the architecture, and the vendor owns the runtime, the tooling, and the release schedule. Main strength: a modern object model and a managed runtime inside the ERP. Main weakness: the platform is the program's boundary.

energy.text: No independent energy or time benchmark for the language is recorded.

ai-readiness.text: Sparse public training data: models write it less reliably than a mainstream language [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: Source compiles in the toolchain release the developer installs
Microsoft documents a deployable package as a binary update for one platform release, and the environment that receives it cannot rebuild it
